scope: Proposition 9.5 (Local root comparison) of the manuscript “Bochner–Riesz multipliers in three dimensions” (preprints/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 078 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ea18d159eefcdc7f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 78. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a winning retained class as above, and use translated coordinates (9.14). Let Kloc 0 be the canonical root supremum of its input, including the norm option. Set AJ = log1/ϵ(N) + 3 2 log1/ϵ(m) + 1 2 g. (9.31) Then, with the error convention (9.25), Kloc 0 ≤ AJ + epkt. (9.32) For any chosen marginal law on the tagged localizers there is an earlier test, using the original input at time r, with score Pall r ≥ H(J) + b∗ + E  log1/ϵ(Nall) + 3 2 log1/ϵ(m) + 1 2 g  − epkt. (9.33) At r = 0, the right hand side is a lower bound for K0 up to the displayed error. The earlier test uses the uniform law on each whole class before the final retained subdivision.
